main_text.p: pellat,& tandem in illas erumpit voces? [tainè monstro me amicum posse fieri calumniator putet? ego admiratione prodigioque calumniæ perculsus, hæsito, quid oporteat respondere, meque in mille mortes condemno, si vel suspitio talis de me uspiam fuerit. Imò tantum abest, ab Imperatore vel armis impetendo, vel lancinando lingua aut calamo; ut passim per eandem Apologiam, se pro eius incolumitate tum priuatim, tum publicè preces fudisse fateatur: nihil aliud dixi, quàm precamur pro salute Reliogiosissimi Imperatoris Constantij,& statim uniuersus populus una voce acclamauit, Christe auxiliare Constantio, & magna perseuerantia has preces continuauit. ] Sed interim alij per Christianum Orbem Episcopi centū & 16. à suis sedibus ex Imperatoris Edicto pulsi, quid meditantur? quid moliuntur? quid Iulius Pontifex Romanus ab Arrianis excommunicatus? quid Liberius amandatus in exilium (legatis suis in carcerem conjectis? ) cur non suum fulmen in Imperatoris caput ejaculatur? imò audi ipsius fulmen in Epistola ad

page.notes: Line 1 begins mid-sentence, so the paragraph continues from the previous page. "Reliogiosissimi" is printed that way (probably for Religiosissimi) and is left as printed. Uncertain: the opening bracket "[tainè" and the reading "tainè". The single paragraph runs to the catchword; no paragraph break is visible. The bracket "]" after "continuauit." is printed as shown. Italic spans: "Constantij," "Christe auxiliare Constantio," "Iulius," "Liberius".
